title: Why Use Fuzzycomplete?
description: Fuzzycomplete replaces DuckDB's built-in [autocomplete](https://duckdb.org/docs/extensions/autocomplete.html) extension with [`code-fuzzy-match`](https://crates.io/crates/code-fuzzy-match) — the same fuzzy-matching algorithm that powers Visual Studio Code. Substring matches, camelCase awareness, and cross-database/cross-schema identifier lookup, all wired into the DuckDB CLI's Tab key.

sections.title: What this extension is for
sections.description: This is a quality-of-life upgrade for the `duckdb` CLI. Once loaded, every Tab-completion in the interactive shell is fuzzy — the same matching style developers expect from VS Code's command palette and symbol search.

bulletPoints.label: Smarter keyword & identifier completion
bulletPoints.description: Suggests SQL keywords and identifiers (databases, schemas, tables, columns) ranked by fuzzy score instead of edit distance. Typing `usrs` finds `users`; typing `gnst` finds `getNotificationStatus`.

bulletPoints.label: Cross-database, cross-schema
bulletPoints.description: Suggestions span every [`ATTACH`](https://duckdb.org/docs/sql/statements/attach)-ed database and every schema on the search path, with the right qualifier prepended automatically — useful in multi-database sessions.

bulletPoints.label: Drop-in replacement
bulletPoints.description: Implements the same `sql_auto_complete` table function as the built-in [autocomplete](https://duckdb.org/docs/extensions/autocomplete.html) extension, so the CLI picks it up without any configuration change.

bulletPoints.label: Zero SQL surface to learn
bulletPoints.description: There's nothing to call from queries. Install, load, hit Tab. Inspect the ranked suggestions with `sql_auto_complete` only if you want to.

sections.title: How the matcher works
sections.description: The Rust crate [`code-fuzzy-match`](https://crates.io/crates/code-fuzzy-match) is a port of the matcher VS Code uses for its command palette and Quick Open. The order of characters in your query has to appear in the candidate, but they don't have to be contiguous — and matches near word boundaries score higher.

bulletPoints.label: Ordered subsequence matching
bulletPoints.description: Every character of your query must appear in the candidate, in order — `usr` matches both `users` and `user_settings`, but not `setUR`.

bulletPoints.label: Word-boundary bonuses
bulletPoints.description: Characters following a separator (`_`, `.`) or at a camelCase word start score higher — `gNS` cleanly hits `getNotificationStatus`.

bulletPoints.label: Sequential-run bonuses
bulletPoints.description: Contiguous matches outscore scattered ones, so `users` beats `u_e_r_s` for the query `usr`.

bulletPoints.label: Tie-breakers favour shorter, lexical
bulletPoints.description: On equal fuzzy score, shorter candidates rank first; ties beyond that are broken lexicographically — so the obvious answer wins.

sections.title: Scope & caveats
sections.description: Honest about what this is and isn't. It's a CLI input-loop tweak — there's no value in loading it from a non-interactive client.

bulletPoints.label: DuckDB CLI only
bulletPoints.description: Tab-completion is a feature of the [DuckDB CLI](https://duckdb.org/docs/api/cli/overview)'s line editor. Loading this extension from the Python / Node / JDBC / ODBC / Rust / WASM clients has no effect on those clients' input — they don't have a CLI line editor to plug into.

bulletPoints.label: Conflicts with the built-in autocomplete
bulletPoints.description: Fuzzycomplete and the built-in [autocomplete](https://duckdb.org/docs/extensions/autocomplete.html) both register a `sql_auto_complete` table function. The last one loaded wins — so load `fuzzycomplete` after any session start-up that auto-loads `autocomplete`.

bulletPoints.label: Suggestions reflect the live catalog
bulletPoints.description: Identifiers come from whatever databases and schemas are currently visible. Newly [`ATTACH`](https://duckdb.org/docs/sql/statements/attach)-ed catalogs become available immediately; nothing needs to be reindexed.

bulletPoints.label: Algorithm choice is a matter of taste
bulletPoints.description: Edit-distance (the default) and fuzzy matching favour different mistakes. If you mostly fix typos, the default may suit you better; if you mostly type partial names, fuzzy matching usually wins.

useCases.title: Long table or column names
useCases.description: Substring matches reach the right identifier without typing the full prefix — `ordit` jumps straight to `order_items` even with dozens of tables in scope.

useCases.title: Multi-database sessions
useCases.description: After several [`ATTACH`](https://duckdb.org/docs/sql/statements/attach) calls, completion respects the search path and qualifies suggestions correctly across every attached catalog.

useCases.title: Code-style identifiers
useCases.description: camelCase and snake_case word starts are weighted properly, so `gNS` lands on `getNotificationStatus` and `o_i` on `order_items`.

useCases.title: Pairing with related extensions
useCases.description: Fuzzycomplete uses the same matching philosophy as [`rapidfuzz`](/products/extensions/rapidfuzz) but at the CLI input layer; for in-SQL fuzzy scoring of strings inside queries, reach for `rapidfuzz` instead.
